verdict.root_cause: cartservice was replaced at 08:01:25Z by an automation-pushed image-reference update to a "hotfix" tag; the running instance shut down gracefully at 08:01:24.9 and no replacement instance ever came back — cartservice emitted no further logs for the remaining eight minutes of the window and produced no span-metric series at all (neither error numerator nor call denominator). With no cart backend listening, frontend's direct CartService/GetCart and AddItem calls and checkoutservice's client-side GetCart inside PlaceOrder fail on the connection itself (a mix of ~3s connect stalls and sub-millisecond immediate refusals), aborting PlaceOrder before payment, currency or accounting are ever called. The failing mechanism is therefore that the artifact now referenced for cartservice is not running/serviceable — a bad deploy — and everything upstream is collateral on that one edge.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent signals converge on the cart edge and on the same minute. Traces (tr_a6b4957d27da) locate the deepest erroring span at the client side of the cart call in every failing PlaceOrder trace, show no server-side cartservice spans anywhere, and show all non-cart dependencies (product catalog, ads, recommendations, feature flag) fast and error-free — which rules out a platform-wide degradation and rules out the unmeasured payment/currency/accounting edges, since those edges are never crossed. Logs (tr_8e77bd20f3da) show cartservice handling normal traffic until ~08:01:22, an orderly hosting-lifetime shutdown at 08:01:24.9, and then complete silence to the window end — no crash, no exception, no redis failure, and critically no startup lines for a successor instance. Metrics (tr_1ad518231fb2) corroborate the absence rather than illness: the calls_total denominator is empty, meaning cartservice is not serving or not instrumented at all, which is exactly the shape a service that is simply gone produces. The change record (tr_e408e150cb41) supplies the act: an image-reference update to a hotfix tag at 08:01:25Z, coincident to the second with the shutdown. Per the taxonomy, an image reference pointed at an artifact that will not serve is bad_deploy even though the reference lives in configuration; the failure is not a wrong address or limit but a wrong/unstartable running artifact. checkoutservice is exonerated as an origin by both its empty change log (tr_fd1169d59f64) and by its PlaceOrder spans being 2-4ms fully accounted for by the failing child call (tr_a6b4957d27da). The intermittency in the frontend and checkout error ratios (tr_3a00c4f73082, tr_b9364622d8c5 — peaks ~38% and ~2/3, floors at zero) is consistent with only cart-touching routes failing while browse traffic succeeds, not with a uniform outage. The corpus's cart-redis-misconfig case is a warning against the inverse read — treating cartservice's zero error rate as health — and here the specialist explicitly refused that inference; the redis-config theory is separately unsupported, since no dependency or connection-setting change is recorded and no cache-client errors appear in logs. The fix that actually resolves this is reverting the image reference to the prior known-good artifact; a restart alone would only re-pull the same tag.
open_questions: The prior image reference is recorded as absent/unknown (tr_e408e150cb41), so the size and content of the delta — and what a rollback would restore to — is not established from the evidence.

No pod- or container-level evidence was collected: whether the new image failed to pull, failed to start, or started and crashed before emitting any log line is unconfirmed. The graceful-shutdown log proves the old instance left, not why nothing replaced it.

The ~3m20s gap between cartservice going silent at 08:01:25 and the first alerts at 08:04:45 is unexplained. It may be alert evaluation delay or client-side caching/retry absorbing early failures, but nothing measured accounts for it.

cartservice request volume and latency before 08:01:22 were never retrieved (tr_1ad518231fb2), so a pre-existing degradation that motivated the automation-pushed 'hotfix' cannot be ruled in or out — the hotfix may be a response to an earlier problem rather than the sole originating fault.
Traces ruled out three of the unmeasured edges by showing they are never crossed (tr_a6b4957d27da); the fourth unmeasured edge named by triage was not identified or examined.

Whether cartservice's own downstream (redis/cache) is reachable for a restored instance is untested — logs only show it was healthy up to shutdown (tr_8e77bd20f3da), which does not guarantee a rollback comes back clean.
